findings.description: The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as literal long-lived static credentials. User data is readable from the instance metadata service (including via SSRF against the internet-facing web server), is returned by the DescribeInstanceAttribute API, and is stored in cleartext in Terraform state.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is present, so IMDSv1 is allowed. On a publicly reachable Apache host this makes SSRF-based theft of instance metadata (including the credentials placed in user data) straightforward.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch = true behind a 0.0.0.0/0 internet gateway route and attached to a security group permitting SSH and HTTP from the entire internet, with no bastion, load balancer, or other network boundary.

No root_block_device encryption is specified, so unless the AMI or the account-level EBS encryption default enforces it, the root volume (which will also contain the user-data credentials) is stored unencrypted.
Ingress allows TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing the administrative SSH service of an internet-facing host to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploitation attempts.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0 and no HTTPS/TLS listener is configured anywhere in the configuration, so all web traffic to the host traverses the internet in cleartext.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, giving a compromised host unrestricted outbound connectivity for data exfiltration or command-and-control.
The EBS volume is created with the encrypted attribute deliberately commented out and no KMS key, so the data volume attached to the web host is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is derived from an unencrypted volume and specifies no encryption, so a full unencrypted copy of the volume data persists and can be copied or shared to other accounts.

The VPC flow log bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration or KMS key, so network telemetry revealing internal addressing, ports and traffic patterns is stored without enforced encryption.

findings.issue_category: no public access block or ACL controls
findings.description: No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or restrictive bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, leaving protection against public exposure of network logs entirely dependent on account-level defaults.
No bucket policy condition on aws:SecureTransport is attached, so flow log objects may be read or written over unencrypted HTTP connections.
force_destroy = true with no versioning or MFA-delete means flow log evidence can be silently overwritten or destroyed, undermining the integrity of security telemetry.

map_public_ip_on_launch = true combined with a route table carrying a 0.0.0.0/0 internet gateway route makes every instance launched in this subnet directly internet-reachable by default, eliminating network segmentation.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true and association with the same internet-gateway route table make any instance placed in this subnet publicly addressable by default.
